candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is epidermal inclusion cyst. A perineural cyst of the pudendal canal is a nerve-sheath-derived cyst arising along the pudendal nerve, not a keratin-filled epithelial inclusion cyst. Although the imaging and anatomical location described (near the pudendal canal, T2 hyperintense, non-enhancing) are more consistent with a perineural or developmental cyst than an epidermal inclusion cyst, the candidate asserts a fundamentally different pathological entity (neural sheath vs. squamous epithelium). The two diagnoses are related in that both are benign cystic lesions in the perineal/pelvic region, but they are incompatible subtypes with different etiologies and histology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Perineural (Tarlov-type) cyst of the pudendal canal is a distinct entity from epidermal inclusion cyst; both are cystic but differ in origin, anatomy, and histology

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of epidermal inclusion cyst appears discordant with the imaging characteristics described (large presacral unilocular T2-hyperintense non-enhancing cyst with pelvic floor neck near pudendal canal), which more strongly suggest a developmental or perineural cyst; reviewer notes possible reference diagnosis error
